classification.difficultyReason: Reduce radical and rational equations to quadratics, then reject candidates invalid in the original equations.

answer.short:
$x=-\dfrac89$.

Isolate the radical, square, factorise and check candidates in the original equation.
answer.worked:
Require $x\geq-1$ and $x+\sqrt{x+1}\ne0$. Cross-multiplying gives
$$\begin{align*}5x-5\sqrt{x+1}&=11x+11\sqrt{x+1}\\6x&=-16\sqrt{x+1}\\3x&=-8\sqrt{x+1}.\end{align*}$$
The right-hand side is nonpositive, so $x\leq0$. Squaring gives
$$\begin{align*}9x^2&=64(x+1)\\9x^2-64x-64&=0\\9x^2-72x+8x-64&=0\\9x(x-8)+8(x-8)&=0\\(9x+8)(x-8)&=0\\x&=-\frac89\quad\text{or}\quad x=8.\end{align*}$$
Reject $x=8$, since it does not satisfy $x\leq0$. For $x=-\frac89$, $\sqrt{x+1}=\frac13$ and
$$\frac{-\frac89-\frac13}{-\frac89+\frac13}=\frac{-\frac{11}{9}}{-\frac59}=\frac{11}{5}.$$
Hence $x=-\frac89$.

answer.short:
$x=2$; $x=\dfrac12$ is excluded.

Cross-multiply, factorise and reject values that make an original denominator zero.
answer.worked:
Since $2x^2+5x-3=(2x-1)(x+3)$, require $x\ne\frac12,-3$. Cross-multiplying gives
$$\begin{align*}2x^2+5x-3&=(2x+1)(2x-1)\\2x^2+5x-3&=4x^2-1\\2x^2-5x+2&=0\\2x^2-4x-x+2&=0\\2x(x-2)-(x-2)&=0\\(2x-1)(x-2)&=0\\x&=\frac12\quad\text{or}\quad x=2.\end{align*}$$
Reject $x=\frac12$, which makes both original denominators zero. For $x=2$,
$$\mathrm{LHS}=\frac13,\qquad \mathrm{RHS}=\frac{5}{8+10-3}=\frac13.$$
Hence $x=2$.
